trap-nonspeakable.notes: FOUR RIGOR FLAGS, in decreasing confidence. (1) SUPPRESS/AMPLIFY INVERTED, verified numerically: the block says hyperbolic knots are states 'where hbar_q^2 suppresses the volume' and torus knots ones 'where hbar_q^2 amplifies the Chern-Simons phase'. At the proton pin hbar_q^2 = 0.009817186, so dividing by it (the hyperbolic case, Vol/hbar_q^2) MULTIPLIES by 101.86 and multiplying by it (the torus case, CS x hbar_q^2) suppresses by the same factor. The two verbs are swapped. (2) THE TRICHOTOMY DOES NOT MATCH THE CASE SPLIT: Thurston's classification is quoted correctly as hyperbolic / Seifert-fibred (torus) / satellite, and the block then says 'The piecewise definition of Geom(K) follows this classification directly'. It does not: Geom(K) has no satellite case, and it has an unknot case that is not one of the three. Satellite knots are therefore undefined under Geom. (3) CS FORMULA UNCITED AND UNBOUNDED: CS(T_{m,n}) = pi^2 (m^2-1)(n^2-1)/(12 m n) is given with no citation and grows without bound (T(2,101) gives 124.6), whereas a Chern-Simons invariant is defined only modulo its period lattice — at best this is a specific lift and should say so. It does have one good internal consistency check: it vanishes at m=1, agreeing with the unknot case. (4) THE PAIRING IDENTITY IS VACUOUS: the displayed 'Frobenius inner product' is literally Geom(K) divided by Geom(K-mirror), so '= 1' follows from Vol(K-mirror) = Vol(K) alone and tells us nothing about the Frobenius pairing or about hbar_q^2 'mediating' it. Minor: torus knots are called 'self-dual under the descent involution', but T(2,3) is chiral, so that phrase needs its involution named. Advisory: the Volume-Conjecture paragraph slides from the coloured Jones at roots of unity to tr_M(rho(B_K)) at fixed q, which are different objects; the VC is itself a conjecture and should be cited as a hypothesis.
